content.title: About
content.content: Saltine crackers are light, dry biscuits made from wheat flour, water, salt and a small amount of vegetable oil. They have a crisp texture, a neutral flavor with a hint of salt, and are often enjoyed as a snack or as a base for toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Saltine crackers were first mass‑produced in the United States in the early 1900s as a long‑lasting snack.
The classic recipe contains no added sugar, making them less caloric than sweet cookies.
They are commonly served with cheese, pâtés, and soups.
In some countries they are called “salty biscuits” or “salted crackers.”
Whole‑grain versions increase dietary fiber content.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The absence of added sugar makes saltines suitable for low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: They provide a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains some fiber
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour they can aid normal digestion.

items.title: Contains salt
items.content: Salt helps maintain electrolyte balance, though intake should be moderated.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Crackers serve as a convenient platform for adding protein (cheese, meat) and vegetables, enhancing overall nutrition.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excessive salt intake may raise blood pressure and strain the kidneys.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional crackers contain wheat flour, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although less caloric than sweet cookies, overconsumption can still contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some recipes may include dairy or soy ingredients that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crackers can be eaten plain, spread with cream cheese, hummus, pâté, or used as a base for canapés. They are often served alongside soups and salads for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store crackers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crispness.
